prompt: Create a clean, realistic photo-style image of a vintage brass-cased mechanical chess clock. It is a single case holding TWO round analogue clock dials side by side, each with a push-button plunger on top. Show a clear mutual-exclusion state: the plunger on the LEFT dial is UP (raised high, sticking up) and the plunger on the RIGHT dial is DOWN (pressed flush). Near the 12 of each dial draw a small red flag: the flag on the LEFT dial has FALLEN to horizontal (out of time), and the flag on the RIGHT dial is still RAISED (vertical). Make the raised-vs-pressed plunger difference and the fallen-vs-raised flag clearly visible on the correct sides. Crisp, clearly readable.
easy_question: This image was supposed to depict an analogue CHESS CLOCK: a single body holding TWO round clock dials side by side, each with a push-button plunger on top. Ignoring artistic quality, does the image actually DEPICT that twin-dial chess clock with a plunger button above each dial? Answer NO only if it shows just prose, a single clock, a blank panel, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_flag: Same chess clock. Near the 12 position of each dial is a small red FLAG. On one dial the flag is RAISED (standing up, vertical); on the other it has FALLEN (dropped to horizontal, sticking out sideways). Which physical side has the red flag that has FALLEN (horizontal): the LEFT dial or the RIGHT dial? Answer with exactly one word: 'left' or 'right'.
reference.q_up_left: Look ONLY at the LEFT dial of this twin-dial chess clock (the dial on the left half of the image). On top of it is a push-button plunger. Is that LEFT plunger raised UP high on a visible stem above the case, or pressed DOWN flush with the case top? Answer with exactly one word: 'up' or 'down'.
reference.q_up_right: Look ONLY at the RIGHT dial of this twin-dial chess clock (the dial on the right half of the image). On top of it is a push-button plunger. Is that RIGHT plunger raised UP high on a visible stem above the case, or pressed DOWN flush with the case top? Answer with exactly one word: 'up' or 'down'.

steps.target: the left push button on top of the clock case (not the red flag)
steps.context: upper-LEFT area of the picture containing the top of the clock case above the left dial and the button standing on it

steps.target: the right push button on top of the clock case (not the red flag)
steps.context: upper-RIGHT area of the picture containing the top of the clock case above the right dial and the button standing on it
